data.description:
Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all. 

Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. 

Job Summary

The Construction Quality Manager is responsible for developing, implementing, and managing the overall Quality Management System (QMS) for large-scale construction projects, ensuring compliance with project specifications, engineering standards, statutory regulations, client requirements, and international quality practices. The role oversees quality assurance and quality control activities across all phases of construction including civil, structural, architectural, mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), process utilities, cleanroom systems, and high-tech industrial facility installations. The position plays a critical role in ensuring defect-free execution, minimizing rework, maintaining construction excellence, and achieving project delivery targets with the highest quality standards. 

Key Roles & Responsibilities

- Develop, implement, and maintain project-wide Construction Quality Management Plans, Inspection & Test Plans (ITPs), quality procedures, and inspection protocols. 
 - Lead all QA/QC activities for civil, structural steel, architectural, mechanical, electrical, instrumentation, piping, HVAC, cleanroom, and utility systems construction works. 
 - Ensure construction activities comply with approved drawings, project specifications, applicable codes, standards, client requirements, and statutory regulations. 
 - Establish and monitor quality assurance systems for contractors, subcontractors, vendors, and suppliers across the project lifecycle. 
 - Conduct quality audits, surveillance inspections, site walkthroughs, and compliance reviews to identify gaps and enforce corrective actions. 
 - Review and approve Method Statements, Material Submittals, Inspection Requests, Test Reports, Welding Procedures, and quality documentation. 
 - Manage Non-Conformance Reports (NCRs), Site Observation Reports (SOR), Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA), Root Cause Analysis (RCA), and quality improvement initiatives. 
 - Coordinate with Engineering, Construction, Procurement, Safety, Commissioning, and Project Controls teams to ensure integrated project execution with required quality. 
 - Oversee testing and inspection activities including concrete testing, welding inspections, NDT, pressure testing, cleanroom validation, and equipment installation quality checks. 
 - Ensure compliance with ISO 9001 Quality Management Systems and applicable international construction standards such as ASTM, ASME, ANSI, NFPA, IPC, SEMI, ACI, AWS, NFPA, FM Global, NEC, IS, DISH, PESO, ATEX, CE, UL and IEC standards. 
 - Shall be developing and implementing Test Protocols for Piping and HVAC in coordination with commissioning team for MEP and other services. 
 - Sustainability shall be conversion with the sustainability and green building requirement. 
 - Monitor contractor quality performance metrics, workmanship standards, punch points, and closure of quality observations. 
 - Lead quality meetings with clients, consultants, EPC contractors, and stakeholders to review project quality performance and risk mitigation actions. 
 - Ensure proper maintenance of quality records, inspection reports, turnover dossiers, as-built documentation, and handover packages. 
 - Support commissioning and startup teams by ensuring all systems are installed and tested in accordance with approved quality standards. 
 - Drive continuous improvement initiatives to enhance construction quality, reduce defects, improve productivity, and optimize project delivery efficiency. 
 - Mentor QA/QC engineers, inspectors, and site quality personnel while fostering a strong culture of quality excellence across the organization. 

Education & Qualifications Required

data.title: ASIC Digital Design, Staff Engineer
data.description:
We Are

Synopsys is the leader in engineering solutions from silicon to systems, enabling customers to rapidly innovate AI-powered products. We deliver industry-leading silicon design, IP, simulation and analysis solutions, and design services. We partner closely with our customers across a wide range of industries to maximize their R&D capability and productivity, powering innovation today that ignites the ingenuity of tomorrow. 

You Are

You have built verification environments that catch bugs before they become customer issues. Whether you have been doing this for three years or closer to ten, you have learned that verification is not about running tests; it is about thinking through what could go wrong and building the infrastructure to prove it won't. You understand that a well-written testbench is half the battle, and the remaining is knowing which corner cases matter, and which ones are just noise. 

You are comfortable working in System Verilog and UVM, writing test cases that exercise real scenarios, not just the ones in the specification. You have debugged enough simulations to recognize patterns in waveforms, and you know when to dig deeper versus when to loop in the design team. Protocols like MIPI UFS/UniPro, DDR, PCIe, Ethernet or USB are not just acronyms to you; you have worked with at least one of them closely enough to understand how transactions flow and where things typically break. 

Working on a verification team means asking questions when the test plan does not make sense, writing assertions that catch issues, and tracking coverage in a way that tells you what you have validated and what you have not. At Synopsys, you will work on IP cores that go into AI systems, automotive platforms, and data centers. The verification work you do will determine whether that IP works when it ships. 

What You'll Be Doing

- Build and maintain UVM-based testbench for RTL IP cores, including agents, drivers, monitors, scoreboards, and coverage collectors
 - Write System Verilog test cases and constrained random stimulus to verify functional correctness across different operating modes and protocol scenarios
 - Develop and execute verification plans based on design specifications, identifying test scenarios, corner cases, and coverage goals
 - Debug RTL and testbench issues by analyzing simulation logs, waveforms, and coverage reports to isolate root causes and verify fixes
 - Implement assertion-based checks and functional coverage models to track verification progress and ensure thorough validation
 - Collaborate with design engineers to understand IP functionality, clarify requirements, and provide feedback on design-for-verification considerations
 - Run regressions, analyze results, and work toward coverage closure, documenting verification status and outstanding issues

The Impact You Will Have

- Ensure Synopsys IP cores are thoroughly validated before they reach customers building AI accelerators, automotive systems, and cloud infrastructure
 - Reduce post-silicon bugs and customer escalations by catching design issues early through systematic verification and coverage analysis
 - Contribute to faster IP release cycles by building reusable verification components and efficient test strategies
 - Help maintain high-quality standards across Synopsys IP products, directly impacting customer success and product reliability
 - Support the development of verification best practices and methodologies within the Bangalore team
 - Enable design teams to iterate faster by providing clear, actionable feedback on functional correctness and edge case behavior
 - Build verification infrastructure that can scale across multiple IP variants and protocol configurations

What You'll Need

- 4-8 years of hands-on experience in ASIC or RTL verification for IP cores or digital designs
 - Understanding of verification planning, test case development, and coverage-driven verification concepts
 - Working knowledge of UVM or similar verification methodologies, with experience building testbench components and writing test cases
 - Solid System Verilog skills, including understanding of constrained random verification, coverage, and assertions
 - Familiarity with at least one industry-standard protocol such as MIPI UFS/UniPro, DDR, PCIe, Ethernet, USB or similar
 - Experience debugging RTL simulations using waveform viewers and analyzing coverage reports to guide verification progress
 - Experience with Perforce or similar revision control environment
 - Basic scripting ability in Python, Perl, TCL, or shell scripting to support automation and regression management
 - Ability to use AI tools like Cursor and GitHub Copilot for analysis, development, debugs and maximizing productivity. 
 - Have good communication skills, will be a team player, and will have good problem-solving skills. 

Who You Are

- You can look at a design spec and start listing the test scenarios that need to be covered without waiting for someone to hand you a complete test plan
 - You are methodical about debugging, when a test fails, you do not guess, you trace through the waveform and log until you understand exactly what happened
 - You ask questions when requirements are unclear or when a design decision seems like it will be hard to verify, and you do it early enough to matter
 - You are comfortable working with design engineers who may be in different locations, coordinating on bug fixes, clarifications, and verification scope
 - You track your own coverage and verification progress, knowing what has been tested, what has not, and what the gaps mean for overall quality
 - You are motivated by the moment when your testbench catches a real bug, the kind that would have caused problems downstream if it had slipped through

The Team You'll Be Part Of

You will join the IPG and SSG Group at the Bangalore Design Center, working alongside verification and design engineers who develop IP cores for a range of applications including AI, automotive, and cloud infrastructure. The team collaborates across Synopsys' global sites, and you will have the opportunity to work on IP that goes into high-performance systems used by customers worldwide. 

Rewards And Benefits

We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

Writing assertions is not a checkbox exercise for you, it is how you encode your understanding of what should never happen. You have debugged enough waveforms to know when something smells wrong three layers deeper than the symptom. 

Leading a verification effort means more than running regressions. You set the strategy, you review the test plans your team writes, and you make the call on what gets verified to what depth. You work directly with RTL designers and architects, not to rubber-stamp their work but to push back when the intent is unclear or the interface is going to be painful to verify. 

At Synopsys, you will work on DesignWare IP that ships into real products. The verification environments you build will be used across product generations, and the bugs you catch will never make it to silicon. 

What You'll Be Doing

- Build and evolve SystemVerilog/UVM verification environments for DesignWare synthesizable IP cores, ensuring they scale across multiple product generations and configurations
 - Define comprehensive test plans that cover corner cases, protocol compliance, and system-level interactions for serial interface protocols and memory controllers, including DDR and LPDDR where applicable
 - Write and debug complex testbenches, checkers, and assertions that catch real bugs in critical PHY blocks and interface logic
 - Develop software requirements for the PHY that scale across various configurations and use cases
 - Own verification closure for multiple critical blocks within DDR PHYs, including functional coverage, code coverage, and formal signoff
 - Collaborate directly with RTL designers, digital architects, and circuit teams to align verification scope with design intent and surface issues early in the design cycle
 - Manage regression infrastructure and work with the infra team to optimize verification cycles, debug failures, and keep the environment reliable

The Impact You Will Have

- Your verification environments will catch critical bugs before tapeout, directly affecting the quality and time-to-market of DesignWare IP used across the semiconductor industry
 - The test plans you define and review will set the verification standard for the team, ensuring consistent coverage and reducing escapes
 - Your coverage-driven approach will surface gaps that others miss, leading to more robust IP and fewer silicon respins
 - The assertions and checkers you write will become reusable verification IP, accelerating future projects and raising the quality bar
 - Your collaboration with RTL and architecture teams will shape design decisions early, making designs easier to verify and more reliable in the field
 - The regression strategies you implement will directly improve team productivity and reduce verification cycle time
 - Your ownership of critical PHY blocks will ensure that high-stakes features meet functional and performance requirements on schedule

What You'll Need

- Bachelor's or Master's in Electrical Engineering or Electronics and Communication Engineering with 4+ years of hands-on verification experience
 - Proven track record leading verification teams through IP project delivery, including planning, execution, and signoff
 - Strong experience developing SystemVerilog/UVM testbenches from scratch and evolving them as designs grow in complexity
 - Deep expertise writing test plans, implementing checkers, and building assertions that catch real bugs, not just toggle coverage
 - Proficiency extracting and interpreting functional coverage and code coverage metrics, and using those insights to drive verification closure
 - Experience verifying serial interface protocols and working through IP design and verification processes, knowledge of DDR or LPDDR protocols is a strong plus
 - Demonstrated ability to own end-to-end verification deliverables, including metric closure and formal review signoff, experience with AI-assisted verification tools is a plus

Who You Are

- You can walk into a coverage review, spot the gap in the test plan, and articulate exactly what scenario is missing and why it matters
 - You write assertions that encode real design intent, not just the obvious cases, and you know the difference between a checker that catches bugs and one that just makes noise
 - You are comfortable leading technical discussions with RTL designers and architects, pushing back when verification scope is unclear or the interface is going to create downstream pain
 - You manage multiple verification efforts in parallel without losing track of what is at risk, what is on schedule, and what needs attention today
 - You debug with purpose, you do not just stare at waveforms hoping for insight, you form hypotheses, test them, and move systematically toward root cause
 - You treat verification infrastructure as a product, you care about regression efficiency, debug turnaround time, and whether your environment is actually usable by the rest of the team

The Team You'll Be Part Of

Your recruiter will share more about the team structure and mission during the interview process. 

Rewards and Benefits

We offer a comprehensive range of health, wellness, and financial benefits to cater to your needs. Our total rewards include both monetary and non-monetary offerings. Your recruiter will provide more details about the salary range and benefits during the hiring process.

data.title: Head of Injection Moulding (Mobile Industry)
data.description:
HEAD OF INJECTION MOULDING

Faridabad, Delhi NCR | On-site | 12-18 years | Reports to the founders Qualification: B. E. / B. Tech or Diploma - Plastics, Polymer, Mechanical or Production Engineering Mobile handset industry moulding experience is mandatory - please read below before applying

Moulding is where our product starts, and where our cost is set. A part moulded badly becomes a part printed badly, assembled badly and rejected at pack - by which point we've paid for all of it. 

You'd own moulding as a function: the floor, the process, the people, the capacity and the capital. That includes overmoulding - rigid shell with soft-touch elastomer - which is a meaningful part of what we produce and a materially harder process than single-shot. 

We are only considering candidates from the mobile handset industry

We want to be direct about this so nobody wastes their time. 

We make small, cosmetically critical parts - sub-millimetre wall sections, visible surfaces with no tolerance for sink or flow marks, tight fit against a device, and cosmetic standards closer to consumer electronics than to general plastics. A part that would pass in most moulding shops gets rejected here. 

The discipline that produces that output is learned in the handset supply chain, and it doesn't transfer quickly from elsewhere. Excellent moulding experience in automotive, appliance, packaging, housewares or general engineering plastics is genuinely excellent experience - it just isn't what this role needs, and we'd be setting you up to struggle. 

So: you should have spent meaningful time moulding handset housings, covers or cosmetic enclosures - at Oppo, Vivo, Xiaomi, Realme, Transsion, Foxconn, Dixon, Lava or in their tier-one supplier base. Adjacent consumer electronics enclosure work at the same cosmetic standard will also be considered. 

The thing that actually limits this floor

We're high-mix. Many moulds, frequent changes, moderate volume per run. In that environment the constraint usually isn't cycle time - it's changeover and the scrap that follows it. Every tool change costs setup hours, then costs more shots before the process stabilises. Across a week of changes that's a serious share of capacity spent producing nothing. 

Most moulding operations measure cycle time obsessively and changeover barely at all. We'd like someone who goes after it. 

What you'd build

- Changeover discipline - SMED method, prepared tooling, parallel setup, and a measured changeover time that comes down
 - Validated parameter sets per mould, so a setter isn't rediscovering the process each time, and a first-off routine that reaches stable quickly and records what stable looked like
 - Material handling discipline - polymer dried to spec before it goes near a machine. Wet resin causes splay and cosmetic defects that get blamed on printing two stations later
 - A skill matrix for setters and operators, with certification before anyone runs unsupervised, and cross-training so capacity doesn't depend on one person's attendance
 - Real downtime and scrap data coded by cause, so improvement has something to aim at
 - Capacity planning and the case for new machines as we grow

You'd own

- Moulding production across shifts, against the plan
 - Scrap and first-pass yield at the machine. Your primary number
 - Process capability, parameter control and changeover performance
 - Machine utilisation, uptime and maintenance coordination
 - Tool condition in production - shot counts, preventive maintenance schedules, spare inserts and components, and escalation to the tool room before a tool fails rather than after
 - Tool repair and refurbishment decisions, with the cost case
 - Moulding capacity decisions and capital proposals
 - The moulding team - setters, operators, helpers, supervisors - including hiring and training
 - Safety, 5S and housekeeping

You need

- 12+ years in injection moulding, with function or plant-level ownership rather than shift supervision alone
 - Mobile handset moulding experience - mandatory. Housings, covers or cosmetic enclosures, at a handset OEM or in their tier-one supplier base. See the note above
 - Hands-on process capability. You can set a machine, read a short shot, and tell a setter what to change and why
 - Defect diagnosis: short shot, flash, sink, weld lines, warpage, splay, burn marks - cause, not just name
 - Material knowledge - PC, ABS, PC/ABS, TPU, PP and filled grades; drying requirements, moisture sensitivity, masterbatch and regrind Overmoulding. A real part of our production and not a side skill: 
 - Two-shot and insert moulding - rotary platen, index and core-back methods, or mould-and-transfer. The machine and tool requirements of each, and when one suits better than the other
 - Material pairing and bond - which combinations bond chemically, which need mechanical interlock, and how melt temperature, shore hardness and surface condition affect adhesion. TPU and TPE over PC and PC/ABS specifically
 - Bond strength as an invisible defect. An overmoulded part can look perfect and delaminate weeks later in a customer's hand. It has to be designed and processed right, because inspection won't catch it. Peel and bond testing is part of the job, not an afterthought
 - Differential shrinkage and warpage between the two materials, and first-shot dimensional stability before the second shot
 - Cycle balancing - the slower shot sets the cycle, which makes process optimisation here a different problem from single-shot
 - Interface flash, colour bleed and the cosmetic defects specific to two-material parts

Tooling, in detail. This is not a nice-to-have for us: 

- Tool construction - mould base and insert construction, steel grades and hardness, cold and hot runner systems, gate types and vestige, cooling layout and what it does to cycle and warpage, venting, ejection, slides and lifters, shut-off surfaces, surface finish and texture
 - Two-shot tool construction - rotation and indexing, sealing at the material interface, second-shot shut-offs, and why these tools fail differently from single-shot ones
 - Tool condition on the floor - reading flash as parting line wear, galling on slides, blocked vents causing burns, scaled water lines quietly adding seconds to cycle, ejector wear, hot runner tip and heater faults. Catching these before they become a stoppage or a scrap run
 - Trials and correction - T0/T1/T2, reading trial results, steel-safe versus steel-removal corrections, shrinkage adjustment, and knowing when a correction is worth doing
 - Repair, refurbish or replace, with the judgement and the cost case behind each
 - The arbitration. The most valuable thing you'll do is decide whether a defect is a tool problem or a process problem. Process people blame the tool, tool rooms blame the process, and the part keeps failing while they argue. We want someone who settles it with evidence
 - Demonstrated changeover or scrap reduction with numbers. We'll ask for before and after
 - Team building across shifts, including developing setters
 - Fluent Hindi; working English

Good to have: tool room or tool design background earlier in your career, scientific moulding or DOE training, multi-cavity and high-cavitation tooling, IMD/IML, take-out robots and automation, SMED implementation, CIPET background, OEE systems. 

Where this sits alongside our Tooling Engineer: they own mould design review and new tool development; you own tools in production - condition, maintenance, correction and when to retire them. You'll disagree occasionally, and that's healthy. 

Tell us: which handset programmes or customers you moulded for, your overmoulding experience and the material pairs you've run, your average changeover time and what you did to it, your scrap rate and how it was measured, one defect where you proved it was the tool and not the process (or the reverse) and how you proved it, and the cosmetic standard you worked to.

data.title: Head of Printing
data.description:
Faridabad, Delhi NCR | On-site | 12-18 years | Reports to the founders Qualification: B. E. / B. Tech - Printing Technology, Polymer or Plastics Engineering, Mechanical, Chemical or Production

Printing is the step that makes our product ours. It's also where most of our quality risk sits, because a defect found at pack is a part we've already paid to mould. 

Your scope is everything that happens to a part after it leaves the tool: UV printing, dye-sublimation, cylindrical and bottle printing, coating, and assembly - through to a finished product ready to pack. 

We have shift managers running the floor, an engineer keeping machines healthy, and a specialist owning colour. What we don't have is anyone accountable for whether our decoration as a whole is good and getting better - or for deciding what we should be able to produce two years from now. 

This role is technical before it is managerial. If you can't stand at a press and tell us why the part in your hand failed, the rest of the job won't work. 

And a large share of the time, the answer isn't the press. Adhesion failures usually trace back to materials - mould release contamination on the part surface, a substrate whose surface energy was never going to accept ink without treatment, plasticiser migrating out of a TPU weeks after it shipped. We want someone who looks upstream before blaming the machine. 

Who owns what - read this

Several roles touch printing, and all of them sit under you: 

- You own the outcome - print and assembly quality, process capability, and what we can and can't produce
 - Operations Managers own daily throughput and dispatch on their shifts
 - The UV Printing Engineer owns machine condition, maintenance and uptime
 - The Colour Management Specialist owns profiles and colour standards

When a defect appears, the diagnosis crosses all four. You decide where it actually came from, what changes, and you're accountable if it comes back. 

What you'd build

- Validated recipes per product and substrate across every process, so output doesn't depend on who's on shift
 - A process capability baseline - what our defect rates actually are, by type and by process. Harder to establish than it sounds, and impossible to improve without
 - A qualification route for new substrates and products, so new product development gets a real answer on printability and assembly rather than an opinion
 - Technology strategy: which process suits which product, where current capability runs out, and what we invest in next
 - A capability roadmap that lets us say yes to work we currently have to decline

Building the team

We're scaling, and most of our operators arrive without print-specific skills. How you build capability matters as much as how you build process. 

- A skill matrix per process - who can set up, who can run, who can judge quality on UV, sublimation, cylindrical and assembly. Certification before anyone operates unsupervised
 - Cross-training as a capacity lever, not an HR nicety. In high-mix production, if one person can set up the bottle line then that line's availability equals their attendance. Depth on every process is how we stop losing days to one person's leave
 - Limit samples, so "acceptable" is a physical object an operator can hold rather than an opinion that shifts by shift. Most quality arguments on a print floor are really definition arguments
 - Train-the-trainer, so capability multiplies rather than routing through you
 - A progression path that gives a good operator a reason to stay beyond the next ₹2, 000 offer
 - The structure of the function itself as we grow - shift coverage, technical specialists, quality

You'd own

- UV flatbed, cylindrical and bottle printing, dye-sublimation, coating and assembly
 - Quality and first-pass yield across the whole post-moulding chain. The number this role is judged on
 - Capacity planning against the production plan
 - Capital decisions for new capacity, and the business cases behind them
 - Customer complaints through to root cause and corrective action
 - The function and its team: shift operations, machine engineering, colour

You need

Real technical depth across our processes. Specifically: 

- Dye-sublimation - transfer printing onto polyester and poly-coated substrates, heat press and 3D vacuum sublimation, and how time, temperature and pressure shift the final result
 - UV inkjet - flatbed printing, LED curing, primer and surface preparation, white ink and varnish layers, and adhesion that holds up weeks later rather than just at inspection
 - Cylindrical and bottle printing - rotary setup, chuck alignment, tapered and non-uniform profiles, maintaining head gap over a curved surface
 - Assembly - multi-part products, fit and tolerance, insert handling, and cosmetic damage prevention on finished parts

Materials - plastics. How substrate behaviour decides what decoration is possible: PC, ABS, PC/ABS, TPU, TPE, PP, PMMA and filled grades. Surface energy and dyne level, and which plastics need corona, plasma or flame treatment before they'll accept anything. Heat deflection limits, which govern what can be sublimated without distorting the part. Mould release carryover, plasticiser migration, and the other upstream causes of a print that fails three weeks later. 

Materials - coatings. Hard coat, soft-touch and PU systems, UV-curable versus two-component thermal cure. Primer and adhesion promoter selection. Mix ratio, pot life and cure schedules for 2K systems. Order of operations - coating over print versus print over coating - and why that choice is rarely reversible. Coating defects: orange peel, fish eyes, pinholes, poor levelling. 

Testing. Cross-hatch adhesion, abrasion, chemical and sweat resistance, and accelerated ageing - enough to establish whether a finish actually holds rather than assuming it will. 

Plus: 

- An engineering degree. B. E. /B. Tech in Printing Technology, Polymer or Plastics Engineering, Mechanical, Chemical or Production. Printing Technology and Polymer Engineering map most closely to this role; a CIPET background is directly relevant on the materials side
 - 12+ years in industrial or digital printing production, with genuine function ownership rather than supervision alone
 - Defect diagnosis you can demonstrate - separating machine, ink, substrate, file, operator and environment as causes rather than guessing
 - Colour management fundamentals, fluent enough to challenge the specialist who owns them
 - Quality improvement with numbers - a defect rate you reduced, and how
 - Equipment selection and commissioning, with capital accountability
 - Demonstrated team building - you've hired, structured and grown a production team, not just inherited one
 - A training system you built, with evidence it worked: skill matrices, certification, limit samples, or whatever you used
 - Leadership across shifts and across technical specialists who know their speciality better than you do
 - Fluent Hindi; working English

Good to have: injection moulding exposure, coating line operation, metals and glass decoration, high-mix short-run environments, screen or pad printing, IMD/IML, drinkware or promotional product decoration. 

Tell us: one print defect you root-caused where the obvious answer turned out to be wrong, one adhesion or coating failure you traced to a material cause, one quality metric you moved with before and after numbers, one operator you developed into something more, and the specific processes, substrates and coatings you've personally run.

data.description:
About Chubb

Chubb is a world leader in insurance. With operations in 54 countries and territories, Chubb provides commercial and personal property and casualty insurance, personal accident and supplemental health insurance, reinsurance and life insurance to a diverse group of clients. The company is defined by its extensive product and service offerings, broad distribution capabilities, exceptional financial strength and local operations globally. Parent company Chubb Limited is listed on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: CB) and is a component of the S&P 500 index. Chubb employs approximately 40, 000 people worldwide. Additional information can be found at: www. chubb. com. 

About Chubb India

At Chubb India, we are on an exciting journey of digital transformation driven by a commitment to engineering excellence and analytics. We are proud to share that we have been officially certified as a Great Place to Work for the third consecutive year, a reflection of the culture at Chubb where we believe in fostering an environment where everyone can thrive, innovate, and grow. 

With a team of over 2500 talented professionals, we encourage a start-up mindset that promotes collaboration, diverse perspectives, and a solution-driven attitude. We are dedicated to building expertise in engineering, analytics, and automation, empowering our teams to excel in a dynamic digital landscape. 

We offer an environment where you will be part of an organization that is dedicated to solving real-world challenges in the insurance industry. Together, we will work to shape the future through innovation and continuous learning. 

Position Details

Job Title: FinLines & Cyber Technology Lead

Function / Department: Technology

Employment Type: Full-time

Location: Hyderabad / Bangalore

Reports To: NA CI Technology Leadership (matrix: Financial Lines & Cyber Lead, US)

Role Overview

We are looking for a FinLines & Cyber Technology Lead who combines deep insurance domain expertise in Financial Lines and Cyber products with strong technology leadership. This is a matrix leadership role, working closely with the Financial Lines and Cyber business lead in the US while embedded within the Chubb India GCC technology team. You will drive technology strategy, platform evolution, and digital capabilities for one of Chubb's most dynamic and fastest-growing insurance segments - spanning Directors & Officers, Errors & Omissions, Management Liability, Employment Practices, and Cyber insurance. This role requires you to be equally fluent in insurance concepts and technology decisions. 

Key Responsibilities

- Serve as the primary technology leader for Financial Lines and Cyber insurance products within the NA CI engineering organisation. 
 - Partner closely with the FL & Cyber business lead in the US to align technology strategy with product strategy, underwriting priorities, and market expansion plans. 
 - Drive platform roadmap for Financial Lines and Cyber: policy administration, underwriting, rating, and claims systems specific to specialty lines. 
 - Lead technology initiatives specific to Cyber insurance - exposure data platforms, threat intelligence integration, cyber risk quantification tooling, and incident response data workflows. 
 - Define and govern integrations between FL/Cyber platforms and the broader Chubb technology estate: reinsurance, finance, claims, and distribution. 
 - Leverage AI and advanced analytics to enhance underwriting decisioning, risk assessment, and claims triage for complex specialty lines - including AI-assisted exposure analysis and emerging risk modelling. 
 - Operate effectively in a matrix structure: influence without direct authority, align teams across US and India, and build trusted relationships with global business and technology stakeholders. 
 - Engage with global architecture, product, actuarial, and underwriting stakeholders to represent FL/Cyber technology needs in enterprise planning forums. 
 - Build and lead a focused team of platform engineers and domain analysts embedded in the FL/Cyber value stream. 

What We Are Looking For

- Strong insurance domain knowledge in Financial Lines - Directors & Officers (D&O), Errors & Omissions (E&O), Management Liability, Employment Practices Liability (EPL) - and/or Cyber insurance products. 
 - Understanding of specialty lines underwriting, policy structures, coverage terms, and claims characteristics that differ from standard P&C lines. 
 - Technology leadership: able to define platform strategy, govern complex multi-system programmes, and engage engineering teams on architecture and delivery. 
 - Awareness of the Cyber insurance technology landscape - risk aggregation tools (e. g. AIR, RMS), cyber exposure data platforms, threat intelligence feeds, and incident response data. 
 - Ability to operate confidently in a matrix structure: influencing without direct authority, managing across US and India time zones and cultures. 
 - Strong communication and stakeholder engagement skills at senior business and technology levels - comfortable presenting to underwriting leadership and technology executives. 
 - Exposure to AI/ML applications in specialty insurance is strongly advantageous: intelligent underwriting assistance, automated exposure analysis, and emerging risk modelling. 

Qualifications

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Business, or a related field. 
 - 15+ years of experience combining insurance domain depth and technology leadership. 
 - Financial Lines or Cyber insurance domain experience is essential for this role - this is a non-negotiable requirement. 

Why Join Us?

- Be at the forefront of digital transformation in the insurance industry. 
 - Lead impactful initiatives that drive engineering excellence and customer outcomes. 
 - Work alongside experienced professionals in a collaborative, innovation-driven environment. 

Why Chubb?

Join Chubb to be part of a leading global insurance company! Our constant focus on employee experience along with a start-up-like culture empowers you to achieve impactful results. 

- Industry leader: Chubb is a world leader in the insurance industry, powered by underwriting and engineering excellence
 - A Great Place to work: Chubb India has been recognized as a Great Place to Work for the years 2023-2024, 2024-2025 and 2025-2026
 - Laser focus on excellence: At Chubb we pride ourselves on our culture of greatness where excellence is a mindset and a way of being. We constantly seek new and innovative ways to excel at work and deliver outstanding results
 - Start-Up Culture: Embracing the spirit of a start-up, our focus on speed and agility enables us to respond swiftly to market requirements, while a culture of ownership empowers employees to drive results that matter
 - Growth and success: As we continue to grow, we are steadfast in our commitment to provide our employees with the best work experience, enabling them to advance their careers in a conducive environment

Employee Benefits

Our company offers a comprehensive benefits package designed to support our employees' health, well-being, and professional growth. Employees enjoy flexible work options, generous paid time off, and robust health coverage, including treatment for dental and vision related requirements. We invest in the future of our employees through continuous learning opportunities and career advancement programs, while fostering a supportive and inclusive work environment. Our benefits include: 

- Savings and Investment plans: We provide specialized benefits like Corporate NPS (National Pension Scheme), Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP), Long-Term Incentive Plan (LTIP), Retiral Benefits and Car Lease that help employees optimally plan their finances
 - Upskilling and career growth opportunities: With a focus on continuous learning, we offer customized programs that support upskilling like Education Reimbursement Programs, Certification programs and access to global learning programs. 
 - Health and Welfare Benefits: We care about our employees' well-being in and out of work and have benefits like Hybrid Work Environment, Employee Assistance Program (EAP), Yearly Free Health campaigns and comprehensive Insurance benefits. 

Application Process

Our recruitment process is designed to be transparent and inclusive. 

- Step 1: Submit your application via the Chubb Careers Portal. 
 - Step 2: Engage with our recruitment team for an initial discussion. 
 - Step 3: Participate in HackerRank assessments/technical/functional interviews and assessments (if applicable). 
 - Step 4: Final interaction with Chubb leadership. 

Join Us

With you Chubb is better. Whether you are solving challenges on a global stage or creating innovative solutions for local markets, your contributions will help shape the future. If you value integrity, innovation, and inclusion, and are ready to make a difference, we invite you to be part of Chubb India's journey.

data.title: Chief Cloud Infrastructure & Security Officer
data.description:
Job Description

Senior Director / Vice President, Cloud Operations & Security Engineering

Location: Chennai DLF

Employment type: Full-time

Experience: 20+ years

Role Summary

Talentgigs is seeking an experienced technology leader to own and advance Production Operations, Cloud Infrastructure, Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), DevSecOps, and Security Engineering. 

This leader will bring deep technical judgment and a strong record of leading cloud-native production environments. They will build a capable, accountable organization that protects and operates critical services through reliable engineering, proactive security, automation, continuous monitoring, and disciplined incident management. 

The role extends beyond traditional infrastructure management and information security management system (ISMS) compliance. The successful candidate will embed security and reliability in engineering and operational practices, reduce risk before it becomes an incident, and use automation and AI-driven operations to improve service health and response. 

Key Responsibilities

Production Operations and Reliability

- Own the reliability, availability, performance, and operational readiness of production services. 
 - Establish clear service ownership, operational accountability, escalation paths, and on-call practices. 
 - Lead incident response, service restoration, root-cause analysis, and follow-through on corrective actions. 
 - Define and improve service-level objectives, service-level indicators, error budgets, and operational health measures. 
 - Strengthen change, release, capacity, resilience, backup, and disaster-recovery practices. 
 - Reduce recurring incidents and operational toil through engineering-led improvements. Cloud Infrastructure and Platform Engineering

- Set the direction for secure, scalable, resilient, and cost-aware cloud infrastructure. 
 - Lead the design and operation of cloud-native platforms, environments, networks, identity controls, and shared services. 
 - Promote infrastructure as code, standard platform patterns, self-service capabilities, and repeatable environment provisioning. 
 - Ensure platform design supports availability, recovery, observability, performance, and secure delivery. 
 - Guide capacity planning, cloud cost visibility, and optimization without compromising reliability or security. SRE and Operational Excellence

- Build and mature SRE practices that make reliability measurable and part of day-to-day engineering. 
 - Develop observability across services using actionable metrics, logs, traces, alerts, and service health views. 
 - Improve deployment safety through progressive delivery, automated checks, rollback readiness, and resilient release practices. 
 - Use incident trends, operational data, and post-incident reviews to guide prioritized improvements. 
 - Create a culture of learning and accountability in which incidents lead to durable fixes. DevSecOps and Security Engineering

- Embed security into software delivery, infrastructure management, and operational workflows. 
 - Lead practical security engineering across identity and access, secrets, configuration, network controls, workload protection, and data safeguards. 
 - Build automated security checks into build, test, deployment, and infrastructure pipelines. 
 - Establish continuous monitoring and threat detection with clear triage, escalation, and response ownership. 
 - Drive vulnerability prevention and remediation through asset visibility, risk-based prioritization, patching, secure configuration, and dependency controls. 
 - Strengthen cloud security posture and address risks across applications, platforms, identities, and operational processes. 
 - Partner with product and engineering teams to resolve security issues early and sustainably. 
 - Ensure audits and ISMS obligations are supported by effective technical controls and evidence, while keeping operational security and risk reduction at the center. Automation and AI-Driven Operations

- Set an automation strategy that reduces manual work, improves consistency, and speeds up safe delivery and recovery. 
 - Apply AI and advanced analytics to suitable operational use cases, such as anomaly detection, alert correlation, incident triage, capacity forecasting, and knowledge retrieval. 
 - Establish appropriate safeguards, human oversight, validation, and access controls for AI-supported operational workflows. 
 - Measure automation outcomes through reduced toil, faster response, fewer repeat incidents, and improved service health. Organization and Leadership

- Build, develop, and retain strong teams across production operations, cloud infrastructure, SRE, DevSecOps, and security engineering. 
 - Define organizational structure, role clarity, decision rights, service ownership, and measurable accountability. 
 - Develop senior technical leaders and create growth paths for engineering and operations talent. 
 - Work closely with product, application engineering, architecture, risk, and business leaders to align technology priorities with business outcomes. 
 - Communicate operational risk, service health, security posture, and investment needs clearly to executive stakeholders. 
 - Lead through technical credibility, sound judgment, collaboration, and consistent follow-through. Required Technical Qualifications

- 20+ years of progressive experience in technology, infrastructure, production operations, cloud engineering, reliability, or security, including substantial leadership responsibility. 
 - Demonstrated hands-on technical leadership in cloud-native production environments. 
 - Strong understanding of cloud architecture, distributed systems, networking, identity, compute, storage, and platform operations. 
 - Experience designing and operating containerized and orchestrated workloads, such as Kubernetes or comparable platforms. 
 - Practical knowledge of infrastructure as code, configuration management, CI/CD, source control, and deployment automation. 
 - Deep working understanding of SRE principles, observability, service-level objectives, incident management, resilience, and disaster recovery. 
 - Experience implementing security controls in cloud and software delivery environments, including identity management, secrets, vulnerability management, secure configuration, and threat detection. 
 - Experience establishing continuous monitoring, alerting, incident response, and security operations practices. 
 - Ability to assess architecture and operational risk, make trade-offs, and guide teams through complex technical decisions. 
 - Familiarity with cloud cost management and capacity planning in production environments. Required Leadership Qualifications

- Experience leading multiple technical functions and managing managers or senior technical leaders. 
 - Track record of building technically strong teams with clear ownership and measurable outcomes. 
 - Ability to stay close to technical decisions while setting direction and enabling teams to execute. 
 - Proven leadership in major incidents, security events, operational change, or complex service transformations. 
 - Strong communication skills, including the ability to explain technical risk and investment priorities to executive and non-technical audiences. 
 - A practical, engineering-led approach to governance, risk management, and compliance. 
 - Demonstrated ability to build trust and work across organizational boundaries. Preferred Skills and Experience

- Experience leading operations and security in a high-scale, high-availability, or business-critical environment. 
 - Experience modernizing legacy infrastructure and operational models into cloud-native platforms and practices. 
 - Familiarity with zero-trust principles, security architecture, threat modeling, and secure software supply chains. 
 - Experience with chaos engineering, resilience testing, game days, and recovery exercises. 
 - Experience using AI or machine learning to improve operational monitoring, incident workflows, or engineering productivity. 
 - Familiarity with security and service-management frameworks or standards relevant to the organization. 
 - Relevant cloud, security, SRE, or leadership certifications. Success Measures

Success in this role will be assessed through sustained improvements in: 

- Production service availability, reliability, performance, and recovery readiness. 
 - Incident frequency, severity, time to detect, time to restore, and recurrence rates. 
 - Adoption and quality of service-level objectives, observability, and service ownership. 
 - Vulnerability exposure, remediation timelines, secure configuration, and cloud security posture. 
 - Security monitoring coverage, alert quality, response readiness, and closure of corrective actions. 
 - Automation coverage, reduction in manual toil, and safe deployment frequency. 
 - Resilience, backup, disaster-recovery, and continuity test outcomes. 
 - Cloud cost visibility and efficiency while meeting reliability and security requirements. 
 - Team capability, role clarity, leadership depth, and accountability across the functions. 
 - The ability of engineering teams to adopt secure and reliable practices as part of normal delivery.

At Baxter, we believe every person-regardless of who they are or where they are from-deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

 - Collaborate closely with software, hardware, and systems teams to support successful product integration and development testing.

 - Provide technical leadership and expertise to help projects achieve key objectives related to quality, cost, schedule, and regulatory compliance. 
 - Contribute to the successful delivery of innovative healthcare solutions by championing best practices in systems engineering, risk management, and product development. 

What You'll Bring

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Software Engineering, Computer Science, Biomedical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

data.title: Platform Engineer - Data Storage
data.description:
At Brevo, we're not just building a CRM. With our technology, we're helping millions of organizations build lasting relationships with their customers. 
From emails and SMS to WhatsApp, Chat, and Marketing Automation, our tools are intuitive, powerful, and built to scale with every ambition. We give businesses a clear view of the customer journey, so they can focus on what matters: connection. 

As a certified B Corp, we're proud to grow with purpose, committed to high standards of social and environmental impact, not just performance. 

Today, more than 500, 000 businesses across 180 countries-from NGOs like Amnesty International to global brands like Carrefour, eBay, Louis Vuitton, and Michelin-trust Brevo to engage their audiences, cut through complexity, and deliver results. Our reliable technology and 75+ integrations help them create unparalleled customer experiences, without the usual tech headaches. 

In 2024, we reached €179M ARR with nearly 1, 000 team members worldwide. And we're just getting started!

Join us as a Platform Engineer to join our dynamic Data Storage team. The ideal candidate will have strong knowledge of database technologies such as Postgres, MongoDB, ClickHouse, etc. , and a strong curiosity to learn how to manage and automate large-scale infrastructure in a distributed system environment.

- Design and implement data storage solutions that meet the performance, reliability, security, and scalability requirements of our software products, using automation tools such as Terraform and Ansible
 - Perform installation, configuration, parameter tuning, and monitoring of database technologies using automation tools like Ansible or Terraform
 - Monitor and optimise performance to ensure high availability and reliability
 - Develop and implement data backup and disaster recovery plans to safeguard against data loss and ensure business continuity
 - Collaborate with internal teams to understand hosting requirements and deliver solutions that meet business needs
 - Participate in automation for deployment pipelines to improve efficiency and reduce manual intervention
 - Help diagnose and resolve production issues, ensuring minimal service disruption
 - Maintain comprehensive documentation of architecture, processes, and procedures
 - Participate in on-call rotations to provide timely incident response and support for production database environments, ensuring rapid resolution and minimal business impact

Who you are: 

- Experience between 4-8 years
 - Must have good knowledge of Linux
 - Must be well-versed in managing any of the data engines: NoSQL, SQL, RDBMS, Object Storage, File Storage (i. e. PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Clickhouse, ScyllaDB, Minio, etc. )
 - Must have a strong understanding of data backup and disaster recovery best practices and methodologies
 - Must have good knowledge of Ansible, Bash or Terraform for automation tasks
 - Must possess excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, with the ability to analyse complex storage issues and develop effective solutions
 - Must be comfortable participating in on-call rotations, taking ownership of production incidents, and responding to critical database issues promptly outside of regular working hours

If you don't meet all the requirements below but believe this opportunity aligns with your expectations and experience, we still encourage you to apply. 
Why people love working at Brevo: 

- A place to grow, together: Join a diverse, international team in a modern office buzzing with energy and ideas
 - Practical perks for everyday balance: Cab Facility and per-day meal vouchers; Employee-friendly salary structure; 1. 4x pay on holidays/weekends for critical work; excellent referral program with high-value gift options (e. g. , bike, flight tickets)
 - Learning, every step of the way: Over 1, 55, 000 courses on Udemy, along with facilitator-led sessions, and personalised training programs tailored to individual and team needs
 - Flexible for life: A hybrid setup (2 days WFH), budget for your home workspace, and a generous leave policy to help you balance life and work effortlessly
 - Wellbeing that works: INR 10 Lakh medical insurance, maternity support, childcare facilities, and wellness bonuses to keep you and your family covered
 - A culture that cares: Annual company off-sites, inter-office trips, team outings, active social, green, and LGBTQIA+ communities, along with festive celebrations - all making Brevo a vibrant and inclusive workplace

Your candidate journey: 

- Round 1 - Screening call with the Talent Acquisition team
 - Round 2 - Face-to-Face Interview with our Deputy Platform Manager
 - Round 3 - Virtual Interview with the Hiring Manager
 - Round 4 - Virtual Interview with the VP of Platform

Whoever you are, wherever you're from, if this role speaks to you, we'd love to hear from you. 

At Brevo, we're proud to be an AI-first company. Still, every application is carefully reviewed by a member of our team.

National : 

National comprises of sector agnostic teams working across industries for a well rounded experience. 

CBS - RM - Proj & Operations : 

EY Consulting is building a better working world by transforming businesses through the power of people, technology and innovation. Our client-centric approach focuses on driving long-term value for our clients by solving their most strategic problems. EY Consulting is made up of three sub-service lines: Business Consulting (including Performance Improvement and Risk Consulting), Technology Consulting and People Advisory Services.

- Infrastructure Automation: Design, provision, and maintain secure, scalable AWS cloud infrastructure using Terraform or CloudFormation. 
 - Container Orchestration & Platform: Manage, optimize, and secure Kubernetes clusters (EKS) for deploying microservices, stream processors, and data connectors.

 - Observability & Reliability: Implement end-to-end monitoring, centralized logging, distributed tracing, and automated alerting using Datadog, New Relic, or Splunk to guarantee high availability for mission-critical integration pipelines. 
 - Data Platform Support: Partner with data engineers to automate, scale, and secure deployments of Apache Kafka, Kafka Connect, Apache Flink/Kafka Streams, and relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle).

Required Qualifications

- DevOps & Cloud Engineering: 5+ years of experience in DevOps or Site Reliability Engineering (SRE), with deep expertise on AWS.

 - Containerization & Orchestration: Proven track record running production workloads using Docker and Kubernetes (EKS).

 - Observability & APM: Strong production experience configuring dashboards, metrics, and alerting in Datadog, New Relic, or Splunk. 
 - Scripting & Tooling: Strong scripting abilities in Python or Bash, with solid understanding of Java/Spring Boot application runtimes and JVM tuning. 
 - Databases & Streaming Awareness: Experience provisioning and supporting self-hosted or managed relational databases (PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, Oracle) and streaming middleware (Apache Kafka).

- Experience managing stateful workloads and operators on Kubernetes (e. g. , Strimzi Kafka Operator, Flink Kubernetes Operator).

 - Keep attrition, absence and engagement at or better than hub targets. Act early on hotspots.

data.title: Solutions Architect
data.description:
About the role

You will be the architect who wins the technical deal. Before a contract is signed, you show enterprise customers that their AI agents will work, at their scale and under their rules. You build the demos and proofs of concept, answer the architecture questions, and hand delivery a plan they can execute. This is a hands-on engineering role in front of customers. You write code most weeks and spend the rest with CIOs, platform teams and risk officers. You report to the Co-Founder and CTO. 

What you will do

• Discover: run technical discovery with CIOs, platform-engineering and risk teams at banks, insurers and asset managers. Map their systems, data and controls to the agent use cases that matter. 

• Demo: build tailored demos of agent workflows, using the customer's own scenarios where you can. 

• Prove: scope and deliver 2 to 6 week proofs of concept. Write the code, wire up integrations and measure results against agreed success criteria. 

• Design: produce reference architectures for agent deployment on AWS, Azure or GCP, covering identity, data access, observability and guardrails. 

• De-risk: answer security, compliance and model-risk questionnaires (SOC 2, data residency, audit logging, human-in-the-loop controls). 

• Hand off: turn every won proof of concept into a delivery plan our forward-deployed engineers can run from day one. 

• Feed back: bring field patterns to product and build reusable demo assets, templates and starter agents. 

What we are looking for

• 8+ years in software engineering, solutions engineering, solutions architecture or forward-deployed engineering for enterprise customers. 

• Hands-on experience building LLM applications or agents: prompt and tool design, RAG, evaluation, and at least one agent framework. 

• Strong Python, plus working knowledge of APIs, containers and one major cloud. 

• Comfort in regulated environments, where governance, auditability and access control decide the deal. 

• Consulting experience: client-facing work, scoping engagements and running workshops with enterprise stakeholders. 

• Understanding of tool calling and MCP, guardrails and policy controls, access management, observability and audit trails. 

Nice to have

• Experience selling to, or working inside, financial services. 

• Kubernetes, observability or AIOps tooling. 

• AWS, Azure or GCP certifications. 

• A public demo, repo, talk or post about something you built with agents. 

Location: Chennai, India (Chennai office), hybrid 3 days on-site, with travel to customer sites as needed. 

About Moring

Moring helps enterprises put AI agents into production safely.

Synchrony's Risk Team provides independent oversight of Synchrony's risk-taking activities to ensure safety and soundness, meet regulatory and legal requirements, and manage risks to the risk-appetite of the Board. Risk is responsible for independently assessing, quantifying, and overseeing risks & providing effective challenge . Risk serves as Synchrony's Second Line of Defense.

Results are consistent with the respective strategic uses and complying with related overall risk, risk testing policies, standards, procedures as well as regulations. Desired Skills/Knowledge

Role Title: VP, eGRC Solution Architect (L12)

Company Overview

Synchrony (NYSE: SYF) is a leading consumer financing company that has been at the heart of American commerce and opportunity for nearly a century. Synchrony delivers credit and banking products that empower tens of millions of consumers to improve their financial lives and access what matters most. Committed to excellence in service and culture, Synchrony is proud to be named as #3 as a Great Place to Work® in India and is honored to be ranked the #1 Best Company to Work For® in the U. S. by Fortune magazine and Great Place to Work®. For more information, visit www. synchrony. com. 

Organizational Overview

Synchrony's Risk Team provides independent oversight of Synchrony's risk-taking activities to ensure safety and soundness, meet regulatory and legal requirements, and manage risks to the risk-appetite of the Board. Risk is responsible for independently assessing, quantifying, and overseeing risks & providing effective challenge . Risk serves as Synchrony's Second Line of Defense. 

Overall, Risk Team oversees and manages the Risk Program to support the business in anticipating and addressing risks, issues and challenges. Results are consistent with the respective strategic uses and complying with related overall risk, risk testing policies, standards, procedures as well as regulations. Our Risk organization consists of 4 pillars: Compliance, Credit & Financial Risk, Enterprise Risk and Operational Risk. Each of the pillars play a vital role in managing Risk and supports the business in anticipating and addressing risks, issues, and challenges. 

Role Summary/ Purpose

The eGRC Solution Architect is an individual contributor who partners with one or more Agile teams within the Risk Infrastructure delivery team to support Risk & Compliance stakeholder s . This role translates enterprise GRC objectives into technology solutions that automate, standardize, and integrate governance, risk management, and regulatory compliance processes. The architect designs end-to-end solutions, decomposes complex objectives into actionable deliverables, evaluates and aligns technical standards and tools, and provides technical leadership across the full delivery lifecycle. 

Key Responsibilities

- Design and deliver GRC solutions: Serve as the GRC technical architecture lead supporting multiple concurrent initiatives, designing end-to-end solutions that span GRC functions, provide design guidance, conduct architecture reviews, and resolving complex technical decisions. 
 - Translate requirements into technical solutions: Work with stakeholders, including Risk and Compliance leaders , to understand GRC requirements and translate them into actionable, technology-based solutions . 
 - Lead technical implementations : Guide and support development teams and related technical resources through the configuration and deployment of GRC software platforms. 
 - Provide technical and architectural guidance: Serve as the subject matter expert for GRC frameworks, processes (e. g. , RCSA, Issue Management, Compliance Risk Assessments), enabling technologies, and industry best practices. Partner with business stakeholders and technical teams to translate requirements into scalable solutions; lead architecture/design reviews; mentor teammates ; and maintain architecture diagrams and technical documentation. 
 - Manage project oversight: Oversee the technical vision of GRC projects, ensuring delivery excellence, security, and sustainability while also managing timelines, scope, and resources alongside project managers. 

Required Skills/Knowledge

- Bachelor's Degree and 10 +years of overall experience or equivalent leadership program experience or in lieu of degree High School Diploma/GED 12+ years of overall experience or equivalent leadership program experience
 - Deep GRC domain knowledge: Strong understanding of GRC concepts and core processes (e. g. , RCSA, Issue Management, Compliance Risk Assessments) and how they align to risk and control objectives . 
 - GRC platform expertise : 5+ years of hands-on advanced configuration/development experience with leading GRC platforms , including ServiceNow IRM, Archer , SAI360 . 
 - Solution architecture experience: 5+ years designing and delivering end-to-end GRC solutions on ServiceNow, Archer, or SAI360, including target-state architecture, standards, and non-functional requirements. 
 - Problem-solving and analytical skills: Proven ability to assess business needs, evaluate risk and control impacts, identify trade-offs, and design scalable solutions that meet functional requirements. 

Desired Skills/Knowledge

- Architectural and technical skills: Proficiency in designing complex systems, cloud environments (AWS, Azure, GCP), and enterprise integration via APIs and data pipelines. 
 - Communication and stakeholder management: The ability to effectively communicate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership. 

Eligibility Criteria

- Bachelor's Degree and 10 +years of overall experience or equivalent leadership program experience or in lieu of degree High School Diploma/GED 12+ years of overall experience or equivalent leadership program experience

Work Timings: 2: 30 PM to 11: 30 PM IST

We are proud to offer flexibility at Synchrony. Our way of working allows you the option to work from home or workspaces in our Regional Engagement Hubs-Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Pune, Kolkata, or Delhi/NCR. 

Occasionally you may be required to commute or travel to Hyderabad or one of the Regional Engagement Hubs for in person engagement activities such as business or team meetings, trainings, and culture events.

data.title: Software Product Assurance Engineer
data.description:
ReOrbit is looking for a motivated and detail oriented Software Product Assurance Engineer for Space Systems to join our growing team. 

As our new Software Product Assurance Engineer, you will play a key role in ensuring the quality, reliability, and safety of software throughout the spacecraft development lifecycle. You will define and evolve software product assurance requirements, adapted to lean and agile development practices, while applying a criticality-based approach where the level of rigour is aligned with the safety and mission impact of each software item. 

You will work closely with software, systems, hardware, AIT, Product Assurance and supplier teams to ensure that software development, verification, configuration management and change control activities meet the required quality and product assurance standards. 

It's an exciting chance to join a dynamic start-up, with the opportunity to make a real impact, to reach our goal of pushing the boundaries of space data transfer. 

Responsibilities

- Define and evolve software product assurance requirements across the development lifecycle, adapted to lean and agile development practices. 
 - Apply a criticality-based approach to software product assurance, scaling the level of rigour according to the safety and mission impact of the software item. 
 - Develop, implement, monitor and review Software Product Assurance (SW PA) plans. 
 - Oversee and participate in verification and validation (V&V) activities according to defined V&V plans. 
 - Support Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) activities, working with IV&V personnel to mitigate software risks and enhance safety and quality. 
 - Help drive internal and external reviews of development plans and software designs to ensure seamless integration with the satellite system. 
 - Participate in the analysis and evaluation of software designs, including change impact analysis and regression testing, particularly for COTS software. 
 - Support Product Assurance activities across engineering and flight models and associated infrastructure, ensuring documentation and objective evidence are captured consistently. 
 - Contribute to estimating and tracking the expected reliability and availability of the satellite platform as part of Product Assurance reporting. 
 - Support Product Assurance follow-up on supplier discrepancies and defects, ensuring corrective actions are documented and tracked. 
 - Support engineering change control, including understanding the Class I / Class II concept and ensuring the required approvals are obtained. 
 - Be willing to travel to supplier facilities for audits when required. 

Skills And Requirements

- Bachelor's or Master's degree in aerospace, electronics, information technology, systems engineering and minimum 8 years of work experience in a similar relevant field. 
 - Knowledge of software development processes and lifecycles. 
 - Knowledge of software verification techniques, including testing and inspections. 
 - Knowledge of software configuration management fundamentals and related tools. 
 - Clear conceptual understanding of the difference between proactive Product Assurance and retrospective Quality Control. 
 - Familiarity with non-conformances, deviations, waivers, and corrective/preventive actions, including RCA and CAPA, at a basic level. 
 - Awareness of SW Product Assurance principles and the ECSS/Q Product Assurance philosophy. 
 - Ability to constructively challenge engineering decisions and ask, "What is the risk?"
 - Comfortable working cross-functionally with systems, hardware, software, AIT and suppliers. 
 - Clear and effective technical writing and communication skills in English, both written and spoken. 
 - Previous exposure to satellite technologies through an internship, thesis, or student satellite project (e. g. CubeSat, nanosat or payloads), with an understanding of software Product Assurance concepts such as verification matrices, test coverage and configuration management. 
 - Introductory knowledge of risk management and single-point failure identification, with proficiency in C/C++ and Python and familiarity with NASA software assurance standards such as NASA-STD-8739. 8 and NASA-GB-8719. 13. 

What does ReOrbit do?

ReOrbit builds the foundation for the next generation of space applications by transforming satellites into truly intelligent, interconnected platforms, defined by software. Our satellite design philosophy revolves around the idea that satellites must network, communicate with each other and thus improve mission efficiency. How can this be achieved? Thanks to a flexible software-first architecture, where all these aspects are dealt with upfront in the mission concept, as integrated functionalities. 

ReOrbit's top-notch team of software engineers and system architects develop in-house software, procure hardware from the best-in-class suppliers, and seamlessly integrate the components to create flexible and secure satellites. Today, we are a rapidly growing company building a very strong multidisciplinary team to support our activities. We are headquartered in Helsinki, Finland with a subsidiaries in Bristol, UK, Bariloche, Argentina and Bengaluru, India. 

Working at ReOrbit

At ReOrbit, we are focused on building a strong team as we believe nothing can be accomplished without innovative, humble and curious minds working together on a common goal. We're all about fostering an inclusive, dynamic environment where equality and diversity are our strength. 

We offer

- Challenging but rewarding environment - you will thrive if you are always reflecting on how to make things better. Your ideas will be heard.

data.title: Principal Engineer - Secondary Design
data.description:
Job Description

The position will lead and guide the P&C design team in delivering project and proposal activities across a diverse portfolio of international T&D, Renewable (Onshore & Offshore wind/ Solar), BESS substation projects, with a strong focus on UK‐based engagements and in addition to providing leadership, the role will also contribute individually to key project deliverables, applying deep technical expertise and established engineering methodologies. 

As a lead, the individual will plan, allocate, and oversee daily tasks within the team, ensuring that all engineering outputs consistently meet required On‐Time Delivery (OTD) targets and comply with internal and external quality standards. The role includes reviewing designs, mentoring junior engineers, resolving technical issues, and ensuring disciplined execution of engineering activities. 

This position is responsible for delivering high‐quality engineering design across multiple concurrent projects ranging from moderate‐scale assignments to major project work packages while ensuring cost‐effective execution aligned with contract specifications, safety requirements, and agreed project timelines. 

The role demands a commitment to technical excellence, proactive team guidance, and a strong focus on quality and timely delivery of day‐to‐day outputs

Responsibilities

To contribute to the technical development and delivery of secondary design within the Renewables power generation team: 

- Evaluates, selects and applies standard techniques and procedures to perform engineering assignments. Prepares project documentation within one's scope of deliverables. 
 - Lead the delivery of Secondary / Protection & Control engineering for EHV/HV/MV substations (up to 400kV) across transmission, distribution, generation, and asset replacement projects. 
 - Provide technical oversight and approval for key deliverables including: 
 - Protection philosophies and schemes (Feeder, Transformer, Busbar, Breaker Failure, Line, Generator, etc. )
 - Protection & Control schematics, wiring diagrams, and panel GA drawings
 - AC/DC system design, battery sizing, and distribution
 - Substation Automation Systems (SAS) including IEC 61850, SCADA, RTU, and telecom interfaces
 - Cause & Effect diagrams, interlocking logic, signal lists, and cable schedules
 - Ensure completeness and functional integrity of assigned work packages and secondary systems. 
 - Review and validate engineering outputs to ensure compliance with: 
 - Client specifications and standards (e. g. National Grid, DNOs, Utilities)
 - International standards (IEC, IEEE)
 - WSP internal quality and assurance processes
 - Resolve complex technical issues arising during design development and execution. 
 - Ensure all inter‐disciplinary interfaces (Primary, Civil, Telecom, SCADA) are properly coordinated and documented
 - Secure the completeness of the assigned packages and correct function of the resulting substation system. 
 - Confirm the engineering is developed, taken into consideration the complete information and all inter discipline checks has been conducted, the results are documented in the project specific storage area. 
 - Solves problems that appear during engineering development. 
 - Focus on cost-efficient and innovative solutions
 - Report and keep records for all engineering changes. Cooperate with the engineering team and agree on the project specific impacts, caused by the changes. 
 - Ensure compliance with Client engineering guidelines, standards and quality across the complete engineering process. 
 - Creates work plans and cost estimates in own area of team responsibility. 
 - Contribute to the risk & opportunity register, by communicating observations. 
 - Prepare all technical documentation for the equipment specification as input to the purchase requisitions

To contribute to the commercial development of Secondary Engineering team:

 - To lead the development and delivery of project proposals; 
 - Lead on efficiency improvements in delivery,

Leadership Skills: 

- Demonstrated ability to lead and motivate a team to achieve goals. 
 - Proven experience in guiding and developing team members. 

Communication:

 - Ability to convey complex ideas clearly and concisely. 

Team Collaboration: 

- Strong team player with the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams. 
 - Foster a positive team environment that encourages creativity and collaboration. 

Qualifications

We'd love to hear from you if you have: 

- Educated to degree level in Electrical Engineering 
 - 12+ Extensive experience in Substation Secondary engineering and interface with other discipline preferably in renewable industry 
 - A wide network of industry contacts and clients 
 - Proactive and highly motivated to meet customer requirements 
 - Proven track record in leading teams 
 - Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, often working on multiple projects/ proposals at any one time 
 - Ability to deliver client work efficiently to externally driven deadlines 
 - Focus on quality, ensuring excellence of deliverables for both project reports and proposals 
 - Strong & in-depth market knowledge of UK Power Industry

data.description:

The team comprises highly motivated engineers and stakeholders who are passionate about extracting targeted insights from diverse document sources and transforming them into high-value data products. Leveraging cutting-edge technologies, the team focuses on building scalable pipelines that efficiently collect, structure, and process large volumes of data. 

Over time, the team has developed a robust and high-performing data pipeline capable of generating best-in-class structured datasets that power FactSet's products. Currently, the team is advancing this ecosystem by driving end-to-end automation across multiple stages of the pipeline. This includes the development of an event-driven, GenAI-centric, agent-based infrastructure aimed at enhancing efficiency, scalability, and innovation in data processing workflows.

Leads development strategies, architecture designs, data management, and code flow analysis necessary for the software development life cycle.  - Cloud (AWS Preferred):

 - Proven experience mentoring software engineers, shaping system design, and driving cross-team initiatives. 
 - Communication:

 - Experience using PySpark for big data ETL/processing, but not a must-have. 
 - Data Engineering: 
 - Familiarity with Spark, Airflow, advanced data analytics stacks, and modern data lakes (e. g. , Delta Lake).
